verdict.line: You lose trades before level 6 if you stand in his Q(Ntofo Strikes)/W(Path Maker) combo range, but the head-to-head is close to a coinflip at 51.3% over 39 games once your core items land.

brief.thesis: K'Sante's W (Path Maker) charge-up and stacking Q (Ntofo Strikes) let him force short, violent trades before Irelia has a reliable answer, which is why he holds both lane and solo-kill advantage pre-6. Irelia's kit doesn't have a hard counter to that burst window, it has a longer scaling curve — Q (Bladesurge) resets and item power catch up by the early-to-mid game, which is why the measured matchup settles back to roughly even.

theirWindow.when: He lands a second Q (Ntofo Strikes) stack
theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks his next Q fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which chains straight into his W (Path Maker) knockback-stun. Don't stand in his short-line Q range back-to-back, and if you're already caught, charge W (Defiant Dance) immediately since it reduces the physical damage you take while charging and blunts that combo.

yourWindow.when: His W and E are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: W (Path Maker, 14-10s CD) is his only stun/knockback and E (Footwork, 10-8s CD) is his only shield/dash — with neither up he has no disengage and no mitigation. Land E (Flawless Duet) for the stun and Mark, then Q (Bladesurge) into him; the Mark refreshes Q's cooldown so you can dash a second time to finish.

powerCurve.note: Neither side has a defining trade tool yet.
W (Path Maker) stun plus Q stacks force bad trades.
His R (All Out) all-in outclasses your first R rank.
BORK and shrinking Q cooldown close the gap.
Full build and passive stacks win extended duels.

start.why: Sustains you through his early Q (Ntofo Strikes) poke; the standard start at 53.3% win rate over 45 games and 97.8% pick rate.

boots.why: He's entirely physical damage between autos, Q, and R-empowered attacks — flat damage reduction beats his poke harder than tenacity does. 56.3% win rate over 32 games, 72.7% pick rate.

core.why: Current-health damage and the on-hit slow give you sustain and stick in trades he's trying to win short.
Scales your single-target duel damage once lane trades stabilize; part of the 61.5% win rate path over 13 games.
Attack speed feeds your passive stacking and the magic resist blunts his R-empowered ability damage.

situational.when: he's building toward extended all-in fights and you need the bleed-and-heal to outlast his R (All Out) burst
you're ahead on kills and want to close out fights faster instead of outlasting him
his damage output is spiking and you need the shield to survive his W/R combo

runes.keystoneWhy: The stacking adaptive force and healing let you win the war of attrition his Q poke is designed to start, and it scales into the extended fights his R (All Out) forces.

summoners.why: The standard pick at 66.7% win rate and 61.4% pick rate. Ignite matters specifically here — it cuts the healing he gets from R (All Out) if you can land a kill window during or right after his all-in.

playing.title: Track his Q stack count
playing.detail: His passive marks you for bonus damage on his next attack, and Q (Ntofo Strikes) builds stacks toward a pulling shockwave at 2 — don't let him land two in a row at point-blank range.

playing.title: Charge W into his poke
playing.detail: W (Defiant Dance) takes reduced physical damage while charging, which directly undercuts his Q/auto poke pattern — use it as a response tool, not just a damage cooldown.

playing.title: All-in only when E and W are down
playing.detail: Without E (Footwork, 10-8s CD) for a shield/dash or W (Path Maker, 14-10s CD) for a stun, he has no answer to your E (Flawless Duet) stun into Q (Bladesurge).

playing.title: Respect level 6 near walls
playing.detail: R (All Out) knocks you through any wall behind you and launches him in after you transformed and healing — don't fight him with your back to terrain once he hits 6.

playing.title: Chain E into Q for resets
playing.detail: E (Flawless Duet) Marks everyone it stuns, and Bladesurge refreshes its cooldown against Marked targets — stun with E, dash with Q, and you can often dash again.

playing.title: Don't force it before level 9
playing.detail: Lane and solo-kill advantage sit with him through level 8 by the data — play for CS and trades off cooldowns, not all-ins, until BORK is online.

playing.title: Play the long game
playing.detail: The 51.3% win rate over 39 games comes from the mid-to-late lane, not the early one — prioritize surviving to your item spikes over winning every exchange.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, and summoner picks are pulled directly from measured OP.GG games on the current patch; the trade windows, tells, and power-curve reasoning are my own read of how the two kits interact.
